source: General Authority of Islamic Affairs and Endowments (Awqaf) timetable, as published by Gulf News
note: Awqaf publishes a genuinely per-city table — not a flat shift off Dubai — so each emirate is checked against its own. Months are kept only where the feed serves the real table: past the published calendar it silently falls back to a generic fixed-90-minute-Isha calculation, which shows up as an Isha-after-Maghrib gap that never varies. Those months are rejected at build time. Each station carries its ground elevation so the regression exercises the terrain correction — the failure that showed up in Al Ain and nowhere else. Single-day spikes in the feed — a value several minutes off both neighbours, which the sun cannot do — are dropped so the regression measures the engine rather than the publisher's typing.
